summary: Between 1965 and 1973 Britain carved the Chagos Islands out of colonial Mauritius and, at US request, secretly expelled the islanders, descendants of enslaved people, so the US could build a military base on Diego Garcia.

evidence.note: US Navy demands in 1965 that the islands be emptied before the base is built
BIOT created and 1965 US-UK deal; slow exile begins by stranding travellers in Mauritius
Foreign Office memos on hiding the islanders' status and denying them citizenship
Islander family descended from people enslaved and brought from Madagascar
Young daughter dies of gangrene after waiting months for a ship; a son dies at eleven
Long segment on the Navy shelling Culebra, Puerto Rico, and the protests that expelled it
Deportees shipped to the Seychelles and held in a prison on arrival
Islanders' dogs shot, poisoned, then gassed with vehicle exhaust and burned
Diego Garcia emptied in 1971, the outer islands by 1973
Base used for the 1973 war, Desert Storm prepositioned ships and alleged torture
Court cases: 2000 ruling, 2004 Orders in Council, 2016 ban, talks with Mauritius from 2022

notes: Part 1 has no transcript; its description says the islands were settled by former slaves, so covered_span starts at the 1783 plantation settlement of Diego Garcia as an estimate (time confidence low). If Part 1 spends little time on that history, the start should move to the 1960s. Mauritius independence (1968) and the Polaris deal were likely in Part 1 but are unverified.
